title: Claude Login Outage Locked Users Out for Two Hours Friday
excerpt: Anthropic's status page logged an authentication incident at 09:58 UTC on November 13 affecting claude.ai, Claude Code, the Console and Cowork, resolved at 11:58 UTC, followed by a separate degraded-performance incident resolved at 15:38 UTC.
body:
• Anthropic logged a login incident at 09:58 UTC on Friday, November 13, saying it was investigating users authenticating to claude.ai and Claude Code, and marked it resolved at 11:58 UTC — about two hours later.
  • Claude.ai was listed as a major outage, the Console and Claude Code as partial outages and Claude Cowork as degraded; the Claude API was not listed as affected in that first incident.
  • A second, separate degraded-performance incident followed the same day on Anthropic's status page, with updates from 13:09 UTC and a resolved note at 15:38 UTC affecting claude.ai, the API, Claude Code and connectors.
  • Anthropic has not given a cause for the login outage. Check status.claude.com first in any future outage — and if you are already signed in, do not sign out to try to fix an error.

Claude locked many users out for about two hours on Friday, November 13, after Anthropic logged a major authentication incident on its status page. Anthropic opened the incident at 09:58 UTC, saying it was investigating an issue with users authenticating to Claude.ai and Claude Code, deployed a fix at 11:05 UTC, and marked the issue resolved at 11:58 UTC. It has not said what went wrong.

The incident, titled “Elevated errors on claude.ai, Claude Code, and platform.claude.com,” was a failure at the front door rather than in the models themselves. Users who needed to sign in — through the website, the coding tool or the developer console — were blocked, while the service behind a valid login continued to run.

What broke, service by service

Anthropic's status page listed four services as affected in the login incident: claude.ai, the chatbot on the web and in the apps; Claude Code, its coding agent; Claude Cowork; and the Claude Console at platform.claude.com, where developers manage accounts and API keys. Claude.ai was marked as a major outage, the Console and Claude Code as partial outages, and Cowork as degraded, according to AI Weekly's account of the status page.

The Claude API itself, at api.anthropic.com, was not on the affected list for that first incident, so applications built by other companies on Claude do not appear to have been hit by the login failure. Third-party reporting put Downdetector reports in India at a peak of 2,906, against a normal baseline of two, at around 3:20 p.m. IST, AI Weekly reported. Anthropic has not said how many people were affected in total, or whether any work was lost.

A second incident the same day

The login outage was not the day's only problem. Anthropic's status page shows a separate investigation into degraded performance beginning at 13:09 UTC on November 13, with updates at 13:52, 14:03 and 14:36 UTC covering claude.ai, the Claude API, Claude Code, connectors including Claude Docs and Sheets, Claude Security and Claude Managed Agents. A monitoring update at 15:33 UTC said errors on claude.ai, including the mobile apps, the API and Claude Code had returned to normal levels, while noting that adding a new connector was temporarily unavailable, scheduled tasks and routines could run more than two hours late with some runs skipped, and Claude Security scans, reviews and project setup remained delayed. The page's resolved note followed at 15:38 UTC, saying the issue affecting multiple surfaces had been resolved.

Readers should keep the two incidents separate. The morning incident was authentication — signing in, or having an existing login checked. The afternoon incident was described by Anthropic as degraded performance across a wider set of surfaces, and unlike the morning incident it did include the API.

Was it the Microsoft outage?

Some coverage tied Friday's Claude problems to the Microsoft 365 outage that began on Thursday and disrupted Outlook and other services. Anthropic has not made that link for the login outage, and nothing on its status page supports it. There is a separate Microsoft-related problem on the page: since 17:52 UTC on Thursday, Anthropic has had an open incident for its Microsoft 365 connector, which lets Claude read mail, calendars, SharePoint and Teams chats, and Anthropic attributes that connector problem to a Microsoft 365 service incident. A connector failure caused by Microsoft is not evidence that Microsoft caused the separate login failure, and this article does not treat it as such.

What to do next time

Check the status page first. If Anthropic has an open incident, the problem is not your account, your network or your country. During a previous sign-in outage in September, Anthropic's advice was that users who were signed in should not sign out; signing out to try to fix an error can leave you locked out until the incident ends. Claude Code users whose sessions dropped should check that changes were saved to their files or repository before continuing.

The outage matters beyond a missed morning of chatbot use because Claude Code and Cowork now carry real working days for many teams, including Indian-origin engineers and firms in the United States and India who build on Anthropic's tools. A sign-in failure shuts out paying users even when the underlying models are running. Until Anthropic publishes a cause, the honest summary is narrow: login failed for about two hours on Friday morning UTC, a broader performance incident followed in the afternoon, both were marked resolved the same day, and the reason for the first failure remains undisclosed.
